statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 16 of 100 in the low band, nine points below the 25 block threshold, while stress stays extreme at 81 and confidence is high at 88.
recommendation: Tail sits in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The decisive evidence this hour is that the roughly 117-point give-back from the session high was retraced rather than extended, which is the signature of a market still granting mean reversion. The named window covers 19:00 to 21:00 UTC, the final cash hour into the 20:00 UTC close on a weekly expiry and the thin post-close futures hour before the 21:00 UTC weekend halt, where conditional tail peaks at 18 and still stays below the watch band. No slot in the forward window reaches the block threshold.
headline: The morning give-back has been bought back without the session high being taken out: NQ trades 29,442.50 at 15:18 UTC inside a 29,120.75-29,500.25 range, roughly 58 points under the pre-bell high, while NDX holds 29,437.84 for a 1.15% gain, VIX is 15.89 after an 10.9% drop and the ten-year sits at 4.936% having spiked to 5.005% on the August CPI report. Tail is 16 in the low band against extreme stress of 81.
body:
Both of Friday's dated U.S. releases are verified. The Bureau of Labor Statistics published the August consumer price report at 12:30 UTC: all items rose 0.4% on a seasonally adjusted basis and 3.4% over twelve months, while all items less food and energy rose 0.3% on the month and 2.4% over the year, with the core monthly figure a tenth above consensus. The University of Michigan preliminary September survey followed at 14:00 UTC at 47.8 against a 51.0 consensus and a 51.7 August final, with year-ahead inflation expectations jumping to 4.6% from 4.0% and the long-run measure ticking to 3.4%.

The price path since the previous assessment is the decisive new evidence. The 13:30 UTC opening auction did not extend the post-report leg: NQ set 29,499.50 to 29,500.25 before the bell, eased to roughly 29,383 by 14:30 UTC, and has since recovered to 29,442.50 at 15:18 UTC, about 58 points under that high, on a session range of 29,120.75 to 29,500.25 against a 29,135.25 prior close. The cash index sits at 29,437.84, up 1.15% from 29,103.51, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,446.24 range. The sequence is a give-back that was granted and then bought, capped by a session high that has held for roughly two hours. That is two-way rotation beneath resistance, not the persistent no-retracement extension that the tail score measures, and it is why tail stays in the low band at 16 rather than rising toward the block threshold.

Internals are aligned to the upside without being one-way. The PHLX Semiconductor Index is 11,879.83, up 2.29%, near its 11,883.14 session high, and seven of the eight largest Nasdaq constituents are higher on the latest available session basis, with Tesla the exception. Volatility is decaying rather than expanding: VIX is 15.89, down 10.94%, having traded as high as 17.71 earlier in the session. Alignment of this kind is treated as a mild amplifier for a possible afternoon continuation leg, not as established structure.

The cross-asset picture is conflicted, which is the reason stress remains extreme while tail stays low. The two-year yield is 4.606%, up 5.6 basis points and at a 52-week high, while the ten-year is 4.936%, marginally lower on the day after touching 5.005% intraday, a flat and hawkish curve response. Reported odds of a 25 basis point increase at the 16 September FOMC rose to roughly 87% to 90% from about 72% a day earlier. Equities advancing more than 1% into a firmly priced rate increase is a conflict signal, and under this framework conflicting evidence raises stress and lowers directional conviction rather than mechanically raising tail. Energy pulled in the relieving direction: WTI is 99.51, down 2.89%, and Brent is 104.76, down 2.67%, though both hold a weekly gain near 9% with the U.S.-Iran tanker conflict around the Strait of Hormuz unresolved.

Ahead of the weekend the structure of the remaining session matters more than its direction. The August budget statement at 18:00 UTC is a low-sensitivity checkpoint. The final cash hour from 19:00 UTC carries the closing auction on a Friday weekly expiry immediately before an FOMC week, and the hour after the 20:00 UTC close runs on thin futures liquidity into the 21:00 UTC CME weekend halt. Those two hours form the named window, with conditional tail peaking at 18. From 21:00 UTC the forward window spends its remaining seventeen slots inside the closure, where no price path can form, so conditional tail falls to the weekend floor and residual risk becomes the gap into the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 15:00 UTC on 10 September to 14:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 14 with the mode mixed and holds a 14 to 19 band through that afternoon, recording event/whipsaw at 19 and 18 in the 20:00 and 21:00 UTC slots around the previous cash close. The overnight hours from 22:00 UTC normalised into an 11 to 15 band, the quietest stretch of the window, with stress pinned in the mid-80s throughout. From 06:00 UTC the mode turned trend-up at tail 13, 14, 13, 14, 15 and 14 as the pre-report advance extended while stress eased from 85 to 81. The two highest readings of the window sit in the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC slots at tail 21 and 22, both event/whipsaw and both mapped to WATCH, spanning the 12:30 UTC consumer price release, with confidence dropping to 70 and 80 as live evidence thinned around the print. The final slot at 14:00 UTC returned to tail 15 and the mixed mode once the opening auction was observed to fade rather than extend, which is the condition that still holds at the start of the current window.
outlookSummary: The forward window covers the remainder of the 11 September cash session and then spends its last eighteen slots inside the CME weekend closure that begins at 21:00 UTC. Conditional tail opens at 16 in the current slot, which contains observed rather than hypothetical structure, and eases through 15, 14 and 14 into the midday lull and the 18:00 UTC budget statement on the assumption that volatility decay continues and retracements keep being granted. It peaks at 18 in the 19:00 UTC final cash hour, where closing-auction and weekly-expiry flow concentrate ahead of an FOMC week, then settles to 15 for the thin post-close hour into the halt. Those two hours form the named window. From 21:00 UTC conditional tail collapses to the 5 to 7 weekend floor because no price path can form while the venue is shut, and conditional stress decays stepwise from 58 into the mid-30s as the live repricing premium is removed. Conditional confidence declines gradually from 88 to 65 with distance from the last verified observation. No slot in the window reaches the 25 block threshold, so every forward slot maps to EA_ON, and the residual weekend risk is carried as a gap into the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen rather than as tail.
